title: bug: moe-agent.sh does not parse under macOS /bin/bash 3.2, so no seat can launch on stock macOS
description:
moe-agent.sh starts with #!/bin/bash, which is bash 3.2 on every Mac. JetBrains on macOS launches agents through this script (TerminalAgentLauncher.kt, ScriptKind.BASH).

**Evidence.** On PR #232's macos-latest CI runner, the moe-account-lease cases that run the launcher under /bin/bash failed with a bash parse error. #232 (fix/ci-pr230) now skips them when bash < 4, with the reason "known launcher bug; remove this skip once it is fixed" (scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs around lines 641 and 748).

**Diagnosis from that run.** bash 3.2 mis-parses a quoted heredoc inside $( ). The culprits are the two JS heredocs:
- MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS at moe-agent.sh:3089 (WT-06, 397fac23)
- MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS at moe-agent.sh:7188 (447281cf)
The other heredoc-in-$( ) sites hold python bodies (2427, 2555, 3883, 5946, 6558, 6683, 6995, 9138). They predate those two and are believed to parse on 3.2, but confirm that under a real bash 3.2 before relying on it.

**Fix direction.** Assign each body outside the $( ), for example a top-level `read -r -d '' VAR <<'JS' ... JS || true`, then run it with node -e "$VAR". Alternatively, ship the JS as a sidecar .cjs next to the script.

This row dependsOn the #232 merge gate (task-d4810c9c), because the bash<4 skip it removes only exists once #232 is on the work branch.
definitionOfDone: /bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh exits 0 under bash 3.2, run on macos-latest CI or a local bash-3.2 build. The command and its output are in the completion summary.
ci.yml runs /bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh on macos-latest, so a bash 3.2 parse regression fails CI.
The bash<4 skip in scripts/tests/moe-account-lease.test.mjs is removed, and the lease cases pass on macos-latest CI.
There is no behavior change on bash 5: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash reports failureClass NONE, and parity-check PASSes.

implementationPlan.description:
scripts/moe-agent.sh: run both node programs outside $( ). This is the fix (DoD 1). Anchor by name, not line: at HEAD 78167a9c, MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS opens in prepare_worktree_launch (~3089) and MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS in prepare_agent_git_guard (~7188).

(a) RED first. Build or reuse the bash 3.2 probe image. Its parts are cached on this host; bash:3.2 = GNU bash 3.2.57, the parser Apple ships.
printf 'FROM node:24-alpine\nRUN apk add --no-cache python3 git ncurses-libs readline\nCOPY --from=bash:3.2 /usr/local/bin/bash /bin/bash\n' | docker build -q -t moe-bash32-probe:local -
Then:
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo:ro" -w /repo moe-bash32-probe:local /bin/bash -c '/bin/bash --version | head -1; /bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh; echo rc=$?'
Expect `syntax error near unexpected token `)'` inside MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS, then rc=2. Keep that output for the completion summary.

(b) Target layout. Each site gets a new top-level function whose body is the existing node line plus its heredoc. Bash's real parser reads a heredoc in a function body fine, even on 3.2, and $( ) only calls the function:

# (one line: macOS /bin/bash 3.2 cannot parse a quoted heredoc inside $( ))
worktree_tooling_node() {
    "$NODE_CMD" - "$PROJECT" "$CLI_ROOT" "$SERENA_PROJECT" "$PREFLIGHT_TASK_ID" <<'MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS'
<JS body, unchanged>
MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS
}

- Site 1: worktree_tooling_node sits above prepare_worktree_launch.
  - Keep the `# prepare_worktree_launch --` header comment directly above prepare_worktree_launch.
  - The `# Design §5.2-§5.4` comment describes the program, so it may move above the new function.
  - prepare_worktree_launch's assignment becomes `out=$(worktree_tooling_node) || worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED` plus the unchanged message.
- Site 2: agent_git_guard_node() goes directly above `prepare_agent_git_guard() {`.
  - Its body: `"$NODE_CMD" - "$PROJECT" "$SECURE_TEMP_DIR" <<'MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS'`, the unchanged JS, `MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS`, then `}`.
  - prepare_agent_git_guard's assignment becomes `AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT=$(agent_git_guard_node) || return 1`.
- Never retype a JS body. Restructure around each body with two small edits, one for the lines above it and one for the lines below it, so the body bytes never pass through an edit string.
- Issue a site's two edits back to back in one response: the file does not parse between them.

(c) Write rule: edit only through a tool the wrapper witnesses.
- Use the Claude Edit tool, which is rename-safe (running sh seats keep their old inode), or a Serena editor from a one-shot seat.
- Never use a shell write (sed -i, python, >, cp/mv). 16 open rows declare this path, so an unwitnessed write is HELD at landing.

The error handling is unchanged by construction. Each function's exit status is node's, so a node failure or a failed heredoc redirection still fails the $( ). The callers' existing `|| return 1` and `|| worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED` still fail closed, so no path launches a CLI without the git guard.

Do not touch any of these:
- moe-agent.ps1;
- the 8 python heredocs inside $( ), each of which was measured alone to parse under 3.2.57;
- any other line.

(d) Tests for this step:
- `bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`.
- The probe command from (a) now prints rc=0. Record it as DoD 1's evidence.
- Both lines of this body check must print. It is the only twin guard for the WT tooling body:
for t in MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS; do diff <(git show HEAD:scripts/moe-agent.sh | sed -n "/<<'$t'\$/,/^$t\$/p" | sed 1d) <(sed -n "/<<'$t'\$/,/^$t\$/p" scripts/moe-agent.sh | sed 1d) && echo "$t body unchanged"; done
- `node --test scripts/tests/agent-git-guard.test.mjs`. Its first case asserts that the sh guard program still equals moe-agent.ps1's.
implementationPlan.note: RED (bash 3.2.57, HEAD before edit): `scripts/moe-agent.sh: line 3125: syntax error near unexpected token `)'` then rc=2. GREEN after edit: `/bin/bash -n` rc=0 under GNU bash 3.2.57 and bash 5 parse OK. Both bodies byte-identical to HEAD (MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS body unchanged / MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS body unchanged). New top-level functions worktree_tooling_node and agent_git_guard_node; callers now `out=$(worktree_tooling_node) || worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED ...` and `AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT=$(agent_git_guard_node) || return 1`. agent-git-guard.test.mjs 25/25 on bash 5. Opener/function counts: 2 functions, 1 opener each. ATTRIBUTION NOTE: peer QA checkpoint baa704f5 (task-7a4aab5e, WT-08) already swept my moe-agent.sh edits into the branch (git diff HEAD on the file is empty); bytes are safe, only attribution is off. Other dirty paths (.moe/tasks/*, scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs, .moe/decisions/) belong to peers and were not touched.

implementationPlan.description:
.github/workflows/ci.yml: make macOS CI parse the wrapper with its stock /bin/bash (DoD 2). In job build-all-platforms, directly after its `- uses: actions/checkout@v7`, add:

      - name: Parse the Bash launcher with the stock macOS bash
        # macOS /bin/bash is 3.2, and JetBrains launches Mac seats through it. Linux and Windows run bash 5,
        # which parses constructs 3.2 rejects (a quoted heredoc inside $( ) is the known one).
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        run: |
          /bin/bash --version
          /bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh

Notes:
- Use the literal /bin/bash. On the macOS image, `bash` on PATH can resolve to Homebrew's bash 5.
- The default macOS run shell stops at the first failing command, so a 3.2 parse regression fails the job.
- Change nothing else. The macOS leg already runs moe-account-lease.test.mjs in `Test agent runtime discovery`.
- Five open rows also declare ci.yml, so step 1's write rule applies.

Test (PyYAML is installed). It prints CI_MACOS_PARSE_STEP_OK; the architect checked that it fails on HEAD:
python3 -c "import yaml; s=[x for x in yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/ci.yml'))['jobs']['build-all-platforms']['steps'] if '/bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh' in x.get('run', '')]; assert len(s) == 1 and s[0].get('if') == 'runner.os == ' + chr(39) + 'macOS' + chr(39), s; print('CI_MACOS_PARSE_STEP_OK')"
implementationPlan.note: ci.yml +8/-0: macOS-only step 'Parse the Bash launcher with the stock macOS bash' right after checkout in build-all-platforms; literal /bin/bash --version and /bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh. PyYAML structural check: RED on the pre-edit file (AssertionError: []), GREEN after (CI_MACOS_PARSE_STEP_OK). Nothing else changed. macos-latest CI runs only on PRs/pushes to main, so the CI run itself is unobserved until the next CI PR.

implementationPlan.description:

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
Chosen: run each node program from a top-level function whose body is the node line plus its heredoc, so $( ) only calls the function. In the prototype the JS bytes are identical to HEAD, the program still reaches node on stdin via `node -`, and the exit status still fails closed.

Rejected:
(1) The description's `IFS= read -r -d '' VAR <<'JS' ... JS || true` + `node -e "$VAR"`.
- `|| true` swallows a failed heredoc redirection. Node on an empty program exits 0 with no output, so prepare_agent_git_guard would hit `[ -n "$AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT" ] || return 0` and launch the CLI with NO git guard. That is fail-open.
- `-e` puts ~5 KB of JS on argv, where Git Bash's MSYS argument conversion can rewrite path-like text.
- It breaks the guard test's `<<'MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS'\n` anchor.
(2) Sidecar .cjs files: two new files that both IDE bundles must ship, while the ps1 twin keeps the inline text the guard test compares byte for byte.
(3) Converting all 10 heredoc-in-$( ) sites: needless. The 8 python sites parse on 3.2.57, and two tests pin STREAM_JSON_PARSER.
(4) Nested function definitions inside the callers: they work, but the file's convention is top-level helpers.

The two node programs (MOE_WT_TOOLING_JS, MOE_GIT_GUARD_JS) moved out of $( ) into top-level functions worktree_tooling_node and agent_git_guard_node; the callers are `out=$(worktree_tooling_node) || worktree_stop MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED ...` and `AGENT_GIT_GUARD_ROOT=$(agent_git_guard_node) || return 1`. JS bodies are byte-identical to HEAD, `node -` still reads stdin, exit status is still node's, so fail-closed is unchanged; ps1 untouched.

DoD 1, GNU bash 3.2.57 (docker bash:3.2 copied into moe-bash32-probe:local as /bin/bash):
- RED at HEAD: `scripts/moe-agent.sh: line 3125: syntax error near unexpected token `)'`, rc=2.
- GREEN: `/bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh` prints BASH32_PARSE_OK, rc=0.

DoD 2: ci.yml +8, a macOS-only step in build-all-platforms right after checkout runs `/bin/bash --version` and `/bin/bash -n scripts/moe-agent.sh`. A PyYAML structural check fails before the edit and prints CI_MACOS_PARSE_STEP_OK after.

DoD 3: moe-account-lease.test.mjs is exactly the reverse of cb3c04af (diff vs cb3c04af^ empty; no bashVersion, bash<4 or known-launcher-bug text). Under bash 3.2.57 the lease + git-guard suites give 65 tests, 64 pass, 0 fail, 1 Windows-only skip, and the six /bin/bash lease cases run.

DoD 4, bash 5: parity-check PASS; lease, git-guard, prompt-cache-launcher and usage-launcher 105 tests, 102 pass, 0 fail, 3 skipped (no PowerShell engine on linux); postflight-safe bash exit 0, failureClass NONE.

NOT observed: a macos-latest CI run. ci.yml runs only on PRs/pushes to main, so the CI step (DoD 2) and the macOS-CI lease pass (DoD 3) are confirmed at the next CI PR; the local 3.2.57 run stands in.

Attribution: a peer QA checkpoint (baa704f5, filed under WT-08) already carried my moe-agent.sh bytes onto the branch; this task's own landing carries ci.yml and the lease test.
